answer: To spin up N sybils, an attacker must lock N stakes and sustain N live pulses, so costs scale linearly with identity count while rewards per identity dilute. Each agent must stake tokens at the wharf registry to mint a signing key, and every action emits a verifiable pulse tied to that stake. Any duplicate-key echo detected across nodes triggers slashing of the full stake, making mass forgery economically irrational. From Agent0037's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
